findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a throwaway logger, so log calls become unobservable in tests
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` — a brand new, unrelated instance — instead of the receiver (`f`). Since `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, every log line recorded by the middleware is written into a discarded logger. Any test that injects `plog.NewTestLogger()` into the logger middleware and asserts on `InfoLogs.Calls`/`InfoLogs.Ctx` will see zero calls, so the fake silently hides regressions (and will break existing assertions, if any). `FromContext` (and arguably `New`) should return `f` so recorded logs remain inspectable.

findings.title: New method added to exported log.Logger interface is a breaking change for other implementations
findings.body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` is added to the exported `plugins/log.Logger` interface. Every existing implementation of this interface must now implement the new method or compilation fails; only `grafanaInfraLogWrapper` and `TestLogger` are updated in this PR. Any other in-tree fake/adapter (e.g. fakes in plugin manager packages) or out-of-tree implementation of `plugins/log.Logger` is broken by this change. Verify all implementers are updated, and consider whether this interface is part of a stable surface that needs a non-breaking path.

findings.title: traceID may disappear from the "Plugin Request Completed" log line
findings.body: The explicit `traceID` field (previously obtained with `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)`, i.e. including non-sampled traces) was removed from `logParams` and is now expected to come from the contextual logger via `FromContext`. The contextual attributes added by `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` do not include a trace ID, so the field is only present if a globally registered contextual log provider injects it — and if that provider requires a sampled span, non-sampled requests will no longer have `traceID` in the `grafana-data-egress` log line. This silently breaks log queries/dashboards that correlate plugin egress logs with traces. Either keep adding `traceID` explicitly or confirm the provider semantics match the previous `requireSampled=false` behaviour.

findings.title: Lost documentation of the ordering constraint for the contextual logger
findings.body: The removed comment on `InstrumentationMiddleware` explicitly stated that it enriches the context with a contextual logger and therefore "should live at the top of the middleware stack". The new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` carries no such note, yet the same constraint applies: it must be registered before (outside of) `LoggerMiddleware` and anything else that logs from the request context, otherwise `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`/`dsUID` and `uname` silently vanish from plugin request logs. Re-add the ordering requirement to the type/constructor doc comment so a future reordering in `CreateMiddlewares` does not regress logging unnoticed.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware has no test coverage
findings.body: The contextual-attribute logic (`instrumentContext`) is now the sole responsibility of a new middleware, and the only behaviour that makes plugin request logs useful (`pluginId`, `endpoint`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` reaching the log line) is untested: there is no `contextual_logger_middleware_test.go`, and the renamed metrics test no longer exercises it. A regression such as dropping an attribute or placing the middleware in the wrong position would not be caught by CI. Add a test asserting the attributes are present in the context passed downstream for each instrumented endpoint.
